# Catalog

# Domain Concept

* [Back styles](backs.md) - The most varied leotard choice: closed, scoop, V, keyhole, clasp-closed high back, strappy, criss-cross, laced/twisted, racerback, open, mesh-filled and asymmetric backs, with exact brand labels, frequency tallies by brand and the rules and practical limits that shape them.
* [Constraints between design choices](choice-constraints.md) - How leotard choices force or rule out each other: high neck forces keyhole and clasp, torso mesh forces lining, sleeve length changes crystal count, strap width and back openings meet rule limits, and ruleset choice restricts sleeves and lettering.
* [Closures](closures.md) - Leotard closures: pull-on (the norm), hook clasp at the back neck, and invisible centre-back zip; which neck and back choices require one, and how often each appears.
* [Current leotard trends (2025-2027)](current-trends.md) - What is in fashion now: NCAA 2025 and 2026 season trends and 2027 predictions (velvet, cuffs, collars, asymmetry, names, sleeve stripes, ribbing) and club-level 2026-27 catalogue trends (ombré, layered mesh, belts, fluoro, heavy crystal).
* [What makes a leotard work (designer guidance)](designer-guidance.md) - Design principles stated by named designers (Jeanne Diaz of GK Elite, Snowflake, Sylvia P) and informed reviewers: function first, lines that hide form breaks and lead the eye up, matte-versus-shine contrast, crystal density, comfort limits, and what to avoid.
* [Fabric zones and panel lines](fabric-zones-and-panel-lines.md) - How brands divide a leotard into named fabric zones (body, sleeves, inserts, belt, straps and binding, underlays and overlays), the design-line types they draw, where mesh goes, the lining rules, device frequencies and fabric durability flags.
* [Garment types and silhouettes](garment-types-and-silhouettes.md) - The base garment choice (tank, cap/short, three-quarter or long-sleeve leotard, biketard, unitard, plus shorts or leggings), how competition and training leotards differ, and how common each sleeve length is by level.
* [Illusion layer (nude mesh)](illusion-layer.md) - How the illusion look is built: skin-tone-lined mesh rising from an opaque sweetheart or V line to a higher mesh neckline, the nude lining tones brands offer, and the open question of how rules treat lined mesh.
* [Leg cut and seat](leg-cut-and-seat.md) - Named leg-cut presets (GK traditional/workout vs modified; Sylvia P standard vs mid cut), the hip-bone ceiling set by rules, seat ride-up as a core fit problem, and leg coverage alternatives.
* [Leotard anatomy and glossary](leotard-anatomy-and-glossary.md) - The parts of a gymnastics leotard and the trade terms used for them (bodice, armscye, gusset, keyhole, binding, rouleau, mystique, sublimation, torso loop and more), with pointers to the concept that covers each.
* [Necklines](necklines.md) - Neckline shapes and finishes (scoop default; V, soft V, square, boatneck-scoop, high/mock neck with neckband or collar, halter, one-shoulder), their brand labels and listing frequencies, and the rule and closure consequences.
* [Sleeves](sleeves.md) - Sleeve options on five independent axes (length, fabric incl. mesh, cap construction, symmetry, surface treatment such as cuffs, stripes and crystals), with brand labels, frequencies and the inner-arm stripe caution.
* [Straps](straps.md) - Strap options by count, width, path pattern, under-layer (skin, nude mesh, printed imitation) and material (binding, rouleau, elastic, mystique); the spaghetti-strap ban, the spotting hazard and the faux-strap workaround.
* [Leotard trends by era](trends-by-era.md) - Historical timeline of leotard design motifs from the 1980s to the Paris 2024 cycle (colour, velvet, keyholes, swirls, mesh, rhinestones, unitards, crystal counts per Olympic leotard).
